mt: 'AMIEL MELBURN TRUST ARCHIVE' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE ARCHIVE AND ITS TRUST AT THEIR GRAIN; THE NEW REASONER LISTED AS A TITLE, THE CRITICS THE PARTY ORDERED SILENT NOT CARRIED
d: THE ARCHIVE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'The Barry Amiel and Norman Melburn Trust runs an online archive of historical socialist and radical writings.' The archive (titles, 1956 to 2024); the trust (history, grants). Six cards: the archive, the trust (three), commonknowledge.coop, Bath and North East Somerset.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the archive, the Overview names its trust, its range and its best-known titles, and the trust's history and grants.
findings: THE TITLES AT THEIR GRAIN. 'It spans nearly 70 years of radical publications, journals, and pamphlets from 1956 to 2024, including prominent titles such as Marxism Today, New Reasoner, Black Dwarf, and others.'

THE ORIGIN OF THE NEW REASONER NOT CARRIED. The archive's own introduction to the title: 'When E.P. Thompson and John Saville were instructed by the leadership of the Communist Party of Great Britain to close down their journal The Reasoner , which had been critical of what the editors saw as the Party’s dogmatism, they refused.' #1725 counts the line from The Reasoner to the New Left as a critique that survived its party by keeping an organ; the composition gives the journal as a title.
THE START DATE KEPT. '1956' is the year of The Reasoner (three issues, 1956, in the archive's holdings list); the composition gives the year without the event.
analysis: An accurate composition of what the archive holds and who funds it. The archive's own account of why its first titles exist, an organ kept by critics after their party ordered it closed, is not carried.

atoms.reference: Runs of journals: The Reasoner, New Reasoner, Universities & Left Review, Marxism Today, Black Dwarf, 7 Days, Red Rag, Soundings and others.
The Reasoner, the journal of two Communist Party members ordered to close it, relaunched as the New Reasoner after their suspension, later New Left Review.

evidence.record_quote: When E.P. Thompson and John Saville were instructed by the leadership of the Communist Party of Great Britain to close down their journal The Reasoner , which had been critical of what the editors saw as the Party’s dogmatism, they refused. Suspended form the party, from which they soon resigned in protest at the Soviet invasion of Hungary, they relaunched with the New Reasoner .
Running to ten issues, the New Reasoner would later merge with the Universities and Left Review and become New Left Review .
